chapter.v:
After this
Job began speaking, cursing the day of his birth.
He said,

“Wipe out
the day I was born, and the night when it was announced that a boy had been conceived.

Turn that
day to darkness. God above should not remember it. Don't let light shine on it.

Take it
back, darkness and death-shadow. A black cloud should overshadow it. It should be as terrifying as the darkness of an eclipse during the day.

Blot out
that night as if it never existed. Don't count it on the calendar. Don't let it have a day in any month.

Let that
night be childless, with no sounds of happiness heard.

Those who
place curses on certain days should curse it, those who have the power to raise Leviathan.

Its early
morning stars should stay dark. Looking for light, may none come, may it not see the glimmer of dawn

for it
did not shut my mother's womb to prevent me from seeing trouble.

Why wasn't
I stillborn? Why didn't I die at birth?

Why was
there a lap for me to lie on, or breasts for me to suck?

For now
I would be lying down in peace. I would be sleeping and at rest,

along with
the kings of this world and their officials whose palaces now lie in ruins,

or with
noblemen who collected gold and filled their houses with silver.

Why wasn't
I a miscarriage, buried in secret, a baby who never saw the light?

There in
the grave the wicked give no more trouble, and those whose strength is gone have their rest.

There prisoners
take it easy—they don't hear the commands of their oppressors.

Both small
and great are there, and slaves are freed from their masters.

Why does
God give life to those who are suffering, living bitterly miserable lives,

those who
are waiting for death that does not come and who are looking for death more desperately than hunting for treasure?

They're so
incredibly happy when they reach the grave!

Why is
light given to someone who doesn't know where they're going, someone God has fenced in?

My groans
are the bread I eat; my raging tears are the water I drink.

For all
that I feared has happened to me; everything that I dreaded has come upon me.

I have
no peace, no quiet, no rest. All that comes is rage.”
